sources.title: A Randomized Trial of Intensive versus Standard Blood-Pressure Control
Dapagliflozin in Patients with Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction
Dexamethasone in Hospitalized Patients with Covid-19

reviewedClaims.text: SPRINT randomly assigned 9361 participants.
SPRINT compared systolic blood-pressure targets below 120 and below 140 mm Hg.
The intensive group had a lower primary composite cardiovascular outcome rate.
All-cause mortality was lower in the intensive-treatment group.
Selected serious adverse events were more frequent with intensive treatment.
People with diabetes were excluded from SPRINT.
The SPRINT intervention was stopped early after a median 3.26 years.
DAPA-HF randomly assigned 4744 patients.
DAPA-HF enrolled patients with heart failure and ejection fraction of 40 percent or less.
Dapagliflozin was compared with placebo in addition to recommended therapy.
The primary outcome combined worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death.
The primary outcome was less frequent with dapagliflozin.
The finding was similar in patients with and without diabetes.
Median follow-up in DAPA-HF was 18.2 months.
RECOVERY compared dexamethasone with usual care in hospitalized Covid-19 patients.
The dexamethasone regimen was 6 mg once daily for up to 10 days.
The primary outcome was 28-day mortality.
Mortality was lower among participants receiving invasive mechanical ventilation.
Mortality was lower among participants receiving oxygen without invasive ventilation.
No mortality benefit was observed among participants receiving no respiratory support.
